pending_commit.commit_message: kukui: scp: set CPU clock to ULPOSC2 SCP CPU clock source can be sourced from 26MHz system clock, 32K low speed clock, and 2 high speed sources ULPOSC1, ULPOSC2. ULPOSC2 is enabled to run at 330MHz by default. This CL switch CPU to ULPOSC2 after enabling the source. BRANCH=none BUG=b:125616659 TEST=manual check current clock source using console command: > rw 0x405C4000 read 0x405c4000 = 0x00000803 Change-Id: I11672e2eb5b5a3ebebdf2a21a6ebed83b4535ee5 Signed-off-by: Rong Chang <rongchang@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1482631 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

camera: Fix clang-format errors After migrating the repo to platform2, we are now using platform2/PRESUBMIT.cfg instead of platform2/camera/PRESUBMIT.cfg. Follow the instruction [1] to fix existing styles before adding camera/ into the clang_format_check list. Third party and machine generated code listed in .presubmitignore are not touched in this CL. CHROMIUM: config: Set mobile lpm policy to min_power_with_partial link_power_management_policy used to be control from user space, but with recents changes: 'commit ebb82e3c79d2 ("ahci: Allow setting a default LPM policy for mobile chipsets")' 'commit b1a9585cc396 ("ata: ahci: Enable DEVSLP by default on x86 with SLP_S0")' The kernel has more control on what is the appropriate LPM policy. Set the mobile lpm policy to min_power_with_partial. AHCI will use it on SLP_S0 capable system. BUG=b:124376423 TEST=On Hatch, check link_power_management_policy is min_power_with_partial with or without charger. Check keyboard resume from suspend works. Change-Id: I771d4e0600768da0e486ad3ca55447bcc536619a Signed-off-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1513161 Commit-Ready: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@google.com> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@google.com> Reviewed-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@google.com>

vboot_ec: always suppress power button on x86 vboot_select_and_load_kernel() disables the power button on detachables, and update_vboot_aux_fw() has analogous functionality to only disable and restore the power button on non-detachables. I've got an upcoming use case that wants to temporarily disable the power button so the status of the button can be queried. This would further complicate the conditions on when to enable or disable the power button. The screen/menu handling in depthcharge already has functionality to monitor the state of the power button for detachables This functionality is also suitable for non-detachables, so this change opts to disable the power button for all x86 boards. BUG=b:124358784 BRANCH=none TEST=build and verified that method can be used to disable and re-enable the power button. Verified that power button can be used at recovery screen and dev screen to turn off Atlas and Arcada. Change-Id: I43fd80fe9adeb797050808ab3b0001fb69abc35f Signed-off-by: Matt Delco <delco@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1470272 Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>

sm: ignore Security Request when Pairing Reqeust is sent Some peripheral devices, e.g., Microsoft Universal Foldable Keyboard, may send Security Request on LE Connection Complete. The host may have sent a Pairing Request when processing the Security Request packet. Per Bluetooth Spec, such Security Request should be ignored and the pairing procedure should proceed intead of going back to L2C_STATE_OPEN. BUG=None TEST=Using a Microsoft Universal Foldable Keyboard for test. Run the command on a DUT: $ ./new_blue_test hidtest "UniversalFoldableKb" It should complete the pairing process correctly. Change-Id: I73d95897f706658d3d48602fe7055cce44de607f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518114 Commit-Ready: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>
